name: Montenegro

paths.name: Holding the portfolio personally
paths.note: Dividends bear 15% personal income tax plus the municipal surtax (17.25% in Podgorica) with a credit for foreign tax up to the Montenegrin tax; capital gains bear a flat 15% with no holding-period exemption. No inheritance or gift tax on movables, no wealth tax.

paths.name: Family holding d.o.o.
paths.note: A Montenegrin d.o.o. owned by the parents holds the portfolio. Foreign dividends and all gains are taxable profit at the progressive 9%/12%/15% rates (the dividend exclusion in Art. 9 covers only Montenegrin payers). Payouts bear 15% plus surtax again. The parents' estate holds the d.o.o. shares; no inheritance tax on movables. Never cheaper than personal holding at the top band: the same 15% on gains, plus a second layer on payouts.

checks.working: Dividends 20,000 of Montenegrin companies (foreign_share 0): personal income tax on capital income 15% (PwC, 'Income determination'; rate raised from 9% by Sl. list CG 152/22) = 3,000, withheld by the payer. Municipal surtax: the municipality may levy up to 15% of the tax in Podgorica (Art. 8(2) Law on Financing Local Self-Government), payable on the tax on capital income (Art. 8(3)); assumed at that cap: 15% x 3,000 = 450. Dividend tax 3,450. Gains 100,000: capital gains tax 15% (PwC; Art. 50a of the personal income tax law, 9% in the 2019 text, raised to 15% by CG 152/22) = 15,000; no holding-period exemption (the exemptions of Art. 37g are the main residence and gifts to first-order relatives, among others; none depends on a holding period) and no surtax, because Art. 8(3) names the tax on capital income, not the separate tax on capital gains. Total 3,450 + 15,000 = 18,450.

Dividends of foreign companies are not excluded (Art. 9 excludes only dividends whose payer is a taxpayer under the Montenegrin profit tax law): 20,000 of taxable profit, in the first band, 9% (Art. 28 para. 2 item 1) = 1,800. Credit for tax paid abroad (Art. 33): the 15% withholding of 3,000 is credited up to the Montenegrin tax on that profit, 1,800, so tax 1,800 - 1,800 = 0; the excess 1,200 is lost. Total 0. Company running costs are not in the tax file. Payout tax excluded.

Gains of 1,600,000 on shares are taxable profit in the year realised (Arts 21-22; no exemption in the consolidated text). Progressive rate (Art. 28 para. 2): EUR 9,000 on the first 100,000 + 12% of the next 1,400,000 (to 1,500,000) = 168,000, giving 177,000 at 1,500,000, + 15% of the 100,000 above = 15,000. Tax 192,000.
checks.model_note: The tax file records one rate per metric (CapitalGains.rates is a single number per asset class), so the engine applies the 15% top rate to the whole gain: 15% x 1,600,000 = 240,000 against 192,000 by the progressive bands.

checks.working: Montenegro levies no inheritance or gift tax on money, securities or other movables; the Law on Real Estate Transfer Tax taxes only transfers of real estate, and the first-order heir and the spouse are exempt even then (Art. 14(1)(1), as recorded in the tax file). The estate is a portfolio of listed shares. Each child receives 3,333,333.33, tax 0. Gifts of capital to first-order relatives are also outside capital gains tax (Art. 37g).

The d.o.o. shares are movable property passing to the three children, as first-order heirs: no inheritance tax on movables, and the first-order exemption would apply to any real estate (Art. 14(1)(1) Law on Real Estate Transfer Tax, as recorded in the tax file). Tax 0.

assumptions: The municipal surtax is taken at the 15% cap for Podgorica, as the tax file does; the municipality sets the actual rate (Art. 9) and the surtax may not reach a shareholder who carries on no activity in the municipality (Art. 8(1)).
Personal gains are taxed at a flat 15% with no holding-period exemption, per the consolidated personal income tax law text read (up to CG 67/19) and PwC for the 15% rate.
The company's 15% foreign-tax credit treats the 15% source withholding as foreign tax on profit (Art. 33).
Checks use top rates for the personal path; for the company the progressive bands are worked as the law gives them.
open_questions: Needs an engine change: the corporate profit tax is progressive (9% to EUR 100,000, EUR 9,000 + 12% to EUR 1.5m, EUR 177,000 + 15% above, Art. 28 of the profit tax law); the tax file holds one rate per metric, so the engine takes 15% for all profit.

Whether the surtax is due after a foreign-tax credit has reduced the personal income tax on a foreign dividend to zero, and whether it applies to a passive shareholder at all (Art. 8(1)), is not settled: the personal check therefore uses domestic dividends only (foreign_share 0).
Whether treaty-limited withholding on a portfolio dividend counts as tax on profit paid abroad under Art. 33 of the profit tax law is assumed, not confirmed.

The profit tax text read is the consolidated version up to Sl. list CG 28/23 (law catalogue PDF); amendments of 2024-2026 were not checked in the Gazette. The personal income tax text read ends at CG 67/19; the 15% rates rest on PwC (reviewed 7 Aug 2026).
Foundation and trust were considered and not added: no family-wealth foundation or trust in common use was found (not researched against a statute).
The real estate transfer tax exemption (Art. 14(1)(1)) and the absence of inheritance tax on movables rest on the tax file's earlier research; the law text was not opened in this pass.
